**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.org_capabilities`

**One row is** One grant or denial, for one org_id and one capability. The org layer: a tenant-wide override of the role default.

WP 2.2 seeded `data_edit_inputs` and `data_edit_policies` into this table from whatever `data_editing` already said, so effective access on the day of deploy was identical to the day before. `data_editing` is deliberately still here: it is removed when the last call site has moved to one of the new keys, not before.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — all carry a predicate |

One of the four layers `capabilities_for_user()` resolves, in the order role -> org -> project -> user, most specific winning. `audited: false` and it matters here more than on most tables: these rows ARE the permissions, and a change to one currently leaves no record of who made it (§2.1 `audit-actor`, WP 2.3).
